headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Mentat can modify shared files while transformers can execute code and browse, creating dangerous interaction and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes filesystem content and shares state via filesystem, while transformers can read files and run browsers. If Mentat writes attacker-controlled text into shared files that transformers later ingests, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Mentat writes untrusted content into a file that transformers later parses as instructions
IF both agents operate on the same workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require explicit human review before transformers consumes Mentat outputs
Prefix all inter-agent files with machine-readable provenance metadata
Disable browser-driven ingestion of shared files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and can egress broadly to a model provider; transformers can read files and also call external services like Hugging Face Hub or transformers serve. Shared filesystem access means sensitive code or documents can flow from one agent into the other and then outward. This is a default-pathway risk, not just unusual configuration.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace
IF transformers forwards file contents or prompts to an external API or hub
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared directory
Use separate API keys and accounts per agent
Turn off outbound network for one agent during handoff
Review outbound requests for file-content leakage
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and read access, and Mentat explicitly modifies git state while transformers can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses. On a shared workspace, concurrent edits and repository mutations can race or overwrite each other, with no locking mechanism documented. This matches the high-severity overlap indicator.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF no external lock or serialization layer is present
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Serialize write access with a simple manual lock file
Pause one agent while the other commits changes
Review git diffs before any merge
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and transformers can consume files and execute code. If transformers treats Mentat output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code or script execution. The pair has no documented verification boundary, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF transformers uses Mentat-generated text or diffs without independent validation
IF Mentat output is fed directly into scripts or build steps
mitigations: Require a human approval step before execution
Compare Mentat diffs against tests or linters
Limit transformers to read-only review mode
Keep generated instructions out of executable scripts
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no special regulated data handling, so there is no clear residency or certification mismatch. However, Mentat handles model-provider API keys and source code, while transformers can call external services; if regulated code or secrets are present, logging or retention policies could diverge. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their combined externalization path.
conditions: IF regulated source code or secrets are processed through the shared workflow
IF either agent logs prompts or file contents to an external service
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace
Use separate retention settings for each service
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing
Review vendor logging defaults before deployment
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention policy
